$comment: Content for Feelings Friends (node g01, ages 3-6): reworked to GDD 01 v2 (mechanic-embodying). "Name
it, and it gets smaller." The very first node and the base for everything: 84 researched scenarios across
six categories, each re-encoded to one of the seven shared v2 play actions (reflect / role-play /
strike-rewrite / branch / sort / match / build): no binary "tap the right card". Affect labelling +
CASEL-aligned SEL; all feelings valid, feeling vs action; both directions (boys cry, girls get angry);
the big "no" + ask a trusted grown-up. Empower never frighten; no WRONG buzzer (reflects have no wrong
answer). Rendered by the shared engine (components/games/v2-engine.tsx).
gameId "feelings": node.game === GameDone key === engine-host id. DO NOT RENAME.
title: Feelings Friends
greet: Hello! I'm Lensy. The Feelings Friends are here, and every feeling is okay. Let's play! 💛

badge.title: Feelings Friend! 🎉
badge.blurb: All feelings are okay, naming one makes it smaller, I can calm the big ones, and saying no and asking for help are brave. 💛

helpLine: If a feeling gets too big, you can always ask a trusted grown-up for help. They want to help. 💛

scenarios.hook: Lensy's Feelings Friends show their faces. Match the face to the feeling.
scenarios.relearn: You can name feelings by looking at faces, happy, sad, angry, scared.

scenarios.hook: You feel something big inside.
scenarios.setup: Name it out loud (it helps!). Say:

yourLine.text: "I feel ___."
Keep it hidden

scenarios.relearn: Naming a feeling out loud helps it feel smaller.

scenarios.hook: Match the moment to the feeling it might bring.
scenarios.relearn: Different moments bring different feelings, all with names.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: how do YOU feel right now?
scenarios.affirm: Thank you for noticing your feeling. That's a real skill.
scenarios.relearn: Noticing how you feel is the first feelings skill.

scenarios.hook: Sort the feeling words by the face they make.
scenarios.relearn: Feelings come in happy ones and harder ones, all are real.

scenarios.hook: More feelings to name! Match face to word.
scenarios.relearn: Tired, excited, shy, all feelings, all with names.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: feelings can be big or small. Can you have more than one at once?
scenarios.affirm: Yes, you can feel two things at once, like excited and a bit nervous.
scenarios.relearn: You can feel more than one feeling at the same time.

scenarios.hook: A Feelings Friend looks sad but says nothing.

yourLine.text: "Are you feeling sad? It's okay to say."
Ignore it

scenarios.relearn: Helping someone name a feeling is a kind thing to do.

scenarios.hook: Match the body clue to the feeling.
scenarios.relearn: Your body gives clues about your feelings.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: naming a feeling is like waving hello to it. Try it, what's here now?
scenarios.affirm: Hello, feeling! Naming it is how we get to know it.
scenarios.relearn: Naming feelings helps you understand yourself.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a feeling, or a thing you DO?
scenarios.relearn: Feelings (angry, sad) are different from actions (hitting, shouting).

scenarios.hook: Build a feelings face for the Feelings Friend.
scenarios.relearn: Faces show feelings; you can read and make them.

scenarios.hook: "Big boys don't cry."

myth.un: Big boys don't cry.
myth.re: Everyone cries; crying lets big feelings out.
myth.why: Tears are for every kid, every gender.

scenarios.relearn: It's okay for anyone to cry.

scenarios.hook: "Good girls don't get angry."

myth.un: Good girls don't get angry.
myth.re: Anger is okay for everyone; what matters is what you do with it.
myth.why: Every feeling, including anger, is allowed.

scenarios.relearn: It's okay to feel angry; we choose kind actions.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a feeling (always okay to have), or an action (you choose)?
scenarios.relearn: Every feeling is okay to have; the action is what we choose.

scenarios.hook: You feel really angry because someone broke your tower.

options.text: Say "I'm angry!" and take big breaths
options.consequence: The anger gets smaller; nobody gets hurt.

options.text: Hit the other kid
options.consequence: Now someone's hurt and you feel worse.

scenarios.debrief: The feeling is okay; the action is your choice. Breathe, don't hit.
scenarios.relearn: Anger is okay; hurting others is not, choose a calm action.

scenarios.hook: "Feeling scared is babyish."

myth.un: Feeling scared is babyish.
myth.re: Everyone feels scared sometimes; it's normal and okay.
myth.why: Fear is your body trying to keep you safe.

scenarios.relearn: Feeling scared is normal for everyone.

scenarios.hook: "Some feelings are bad feelings."

myth.un: Some feelings are bad feelings.
myth.re: There are no bad feelings, just feelings; it's actions that can be unkind.
myth.why: A feeling by itself never hurts anyone.

scenarios.relearn: There are no bad feelings; only kind or unkind actions.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a kind way, or unkind way, to show anger?
scenarios.relearn: You can show anger in kind ways: name it, breathe, take a break.

scenarios.hook: You feel a big feeling and want to let it out safely.

yourLine.text: "I feel ___, and that's okay."
"I shouldn't feel this."

scenarios.relearn: Saying 'I feel ___ and that's okay' helps the feeling settle.

scenarios.hook: "You should hide your feelings."

myth.un: You should hide your feelings.
myth.re: Sharing feelings with someone you trust helps.
myth.why: Hidden feelings get heavier; shared ones get lighter.

scenarios.relearn: It's good to share feelings with someone you trust.

scenarios.hook: You feel jealous when your friend gets a new toy.

options.text: Notice it: "I feel jealous, that's okay"
options.consequence: Naming it helps; you can still be happy for them.

options.text: Grab their toy
options.consequence: Your friend's upset and you still feel bad.

scenarios.debrief: Jealousy is okay to feel; naming it beats acting on it.
scenarios.relearn: It's okay to feel jealous; name it instead of grabbing.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: even Lensy feels scared sometimes. Does everyone?
scenarios.affirm: Yes, every single person feels every kind of feeling sometimes.
scenarios.relearn: Everyone, even grown-ups, feels all the feelings sometimes.

scenarios.hook: Match the okay-feeling to a kind thing to do with it.
scenarios.relearn: Every feeling has a kind, safe thing you can do with it.

scenarios.hook: A big feeling is bubbling up. Let's calm it.
scenarios.setup: Breathe with Lensy. Say and do:

yourLine.text: "Smell the flower... blow the candle..." (slow breaths)
Hold my breath and tense up

scenarios.relearn: Slow breaths (smell the flower, blow the candle) calm big feelings.

scenarios.hook: Build your calm-down kit.
scenarios.prompt: Add things that help you feel calm.
scenarios.relearn: Your calm-down kit: breaths, a hug, counting, a quiet spot.

scenarios.hook: You're so angry you want to explode.

options.text: Take five big breaths first
options.consequence: The big feeling shrinks enough to think.

options.text: Shout and stomp at everyone
options.consequence: The feeling stays big and others get upset.

scenarios.debrief: Breaths first; they make the big feeling smaller.
scenarios.relearn: Big breaths help before you do anything else.

scenarios.hook: Sort: helps you calm down, or makes it bigger?
scenarios.relearn: Breaths, cuddles, and counting calm big feelings; hitting and screaming don't.

scenarios.hook: You need a moment to feel better.
scenarios.setup: Ask for what you need. Say:

yourLine.text: "I need a little break, please."
Bottle it all up

scenarios.relearn: Asking for a break is a smart way to handle big feelings.

scenarios.hook: Match the big feeling to a calming move.

pairs.right: Take a break, then try again

scenarios.relearn: Different big feelings have calming moves that help.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: what helps YOU feel calm?
scenarios.affirm: That's a great calmer. Keep it ready for big-feeling moments.
scenarios.relearn: Knowing what calms you is a feelings superpower.

scenarios.hook: Build a 'calm corner' for the classroom.
scenarios.relearn: A calm corner is a kind place to settle big feelings.

scenarios.hook: Your friend is having a big-feeling meltdown.

options.text: Stay calm and offer them a breath or space
options.consequence: They start to settle; you helped.

options.text: Yell at them to stop
options.consequence: They get more upset.

scenarios.debrief: Calm helps calm; offer a breath or some space.
scenarios.relearn: You can help a friend calm down by staying gentle.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: after you calm down, the feeling is still there but smaller. Notice that?
scenarios.affirm: Yes, calming doesn't erase the feeling; it makes it small enough to handle.
scenarios.relearn: Calming makes a big feeling small enough to handle.

scenarios.hook: A friend is crying because they fell down.

options.text: Go over and ask "are you okay?"
options.consequence: They feel cared for and calmer.

options.text: Walk past
options.consequence: They feel alone with the hurt.

scenarios.debrief: Noticing and caring is what feelings friends do.
scenarios.relearn: When someone's sad, asking "are you okay?" helps a lot.

scenarios.hook: Read your friends' faces. Match face to feeling.
scenarios.relearn: Reading faces and bodies helps you know how a friend feels.

scenarios.hook: A new kid looks nervous and alone on the first day.

options.text: Smile and say "want to play with me?"
options.consequence: They relax; you made the day better.

options.text: Leave them be
options.consequence: They stay nervous and lonely.

scenarios.debrief: A small kindness can change how someone feels.
scenarios.relearn: You can help someone's nervous feeling with a friendly hello.

scenarios.hook: A friend tells you they're sad.

yourLine.text: "That sounds hard. I'm here."
"Stop being sad."

scenarios.relearn: Caring words like "I'm here" help a sad friend feel less alone.

scenarios.hook: Sort: helps a sad friend, or doesn't?
scenarios.relearn: Sitting close, a hug and asking "are you okay?" help; laughing doesn't.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: when someone is happy, how can you join their feeling?
scenarios.affirm: Sharing happy feelings makes them even bigger. Lovely.
scenarios.relearn: You can share in others' happy feelings too.

scenarios.hook: Your sibling is scared of the dark at bedtime.

options.text: Say "I get scared too sometimes, I'm here"
options.consequence: They feel understood and braver.

options.text: Call them a baby
options.consequence: They feel ashamed and more scared.

scenarios.debrief: Sharing that you feel things too helps others feel safe.
scenarios.relearn: Telling someone "me too" helps their scared feeling.

scenarios.hook: Match the friend's feeling to a kind helper-action.
scenarios.relearn: Each feeling a friend has, has a kind way you can help.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: being a good feelings friend means noticing others. Can you?
scenarios.affirm: Noticing how others feel is a wonderful, kind skill.
scenarios.relearn: Noticing others' feelings is part of being a kind friend.

scenarios.hook: Someone is doing something you don't like.

yourLine.text: "No! I don't like that."
Stay quiet and feel bad

scenarios.relearn: Your big 'no' is strong and okay to use (links My Body, My Rules).

scenarios.hook: You feel scared and don't know what to do.

options.text: Go tell a trusted grown-up
options.consequence: They help you feel safe.

options.text: Keep it to yourself
options.consequence: The scared feeling stays heavy and alone.

scenarios.debrief: Telling a trusted grown-up is what to do with a scared feeling.
scenarios.relearn: When you're scared, tell a trusted grown-up.

scenarios.hook: "Asking for help means you're weak."

myth.un: Asking for help means you're weak.
myth.re: Asking for help is smart and brave.
myth.why: Everyone needs help sometimes.

scenarios.relearn: Asking for help is a brave, smart thing to do.

scenarios.hook: Build your list of trusted grown-ups to tell.
scenarios.prompt: Add grown-ups who help you feel safe.
scenarios.relearn: Knowing who you can tell helps with big or scary feelings.

scenarios.hook: You're feeling too much and need a grown-up.

yourLine.text: "I need help with a big feeling."
Say nothing

scenarios.relearn: You can ask a grown-up for help with feelings, not just scrapes.

scenarios.hook: A bigger kid is doing something that makes you uncomfortable.

options.text: Say "no", walk away, and tell a trusted grown-up
options.consequence: You stay safe and get help.

options.text: Freeze and say nothing
options.consequence: It might keep happening; telling helps it stop.

scenarios.debrief: No, go, tell, that's how to handle an uncomfortable feeling with someone.
scenarios.relearn: Say no, walk away, and tell a trusted grown-up.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a good way to handle a too-big feeling, or not?

items.text: Keep it a secret and worry alone

scenarios.relearn: Telling someone, asking for comfort and breathing help; hiding and lashing out don't.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: it's brave to say 'no' and brave to ask for help. Agree?
scenarios.affirm: Yes, saying no and asking for help are both brave and strong.
scenarios.relearn: Saying no and asking for help are both brave.

scenarios.hook: A grown-up you trust asks how you're feeling.

yourLine.text: "Actually, I feel ___ today."
"Fine" (when you're not)

scenarios.relearn: Telling a trusted grown-up how you really feel helps.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: which Feelings Friend feels most like you today?
scenarios.affirm: Thanks for sharing. However you feel today, it's okay.
scenarios.relearn: Checking in on your own feeling is a daily superpower.

scenarios.hook: Build your own Feelings Friend.
scenarios.prompt: Give them a feeling and a calmer.
scenarios.relearn: Your Feelings Friend knows: name it, calm it, get help, say no.

scenarios.hook: "Some feelings should never be shown."

myth.un: Some feelings should never be shown.
myth.re: All feelings can be shown in kind, safe ways.
myth.why: Showing feelings safely is healthy.

scenarios.relearn: All feelings can be shown safely and kindly.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: feelings come and go, like weather. Does a feeling last forever?
scenarios.affirm: Feelings pass, like weather. Even big ones get smaller with time.
scenarios.relearn: Feelings pass; even big ones get smaller over time.

scenarios.hook: You had a hard feeling and handled it well.

yourLine.text: "I named it, I calmed it, well done me!"
"I'm bad at feelings."

scenarios.relearn: You can be proud when you handle a big feeling well.

scenarios.hook: You wake up grumpy for no clear reason.

options.text: Name it: "I feel grumpy" and be gentle with yourself
options.consequence: Naming it helps; the grump softens.

options.text: Be mean to everyone
options.consequence: The grump spreads and grows.

scenarios.debrief: Even mystery feelings get smaller when you name them.
scenarios.relearn: Name a grumpy feeling and be gentle with yourself.

scenarios.hook: Match the feelings skill to what it does.
scenarios.relearn: Name it, calm it, share it, breathe, and wait, your feelings skills.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: you're a Feelings Friend now. What will you remember?
scenarios.affirm: Carry that. You know how to be a great friend to your feelings.
scenarios.relearn: Name feelings, all are okay, calm the big ones, say no, ask for help.

scenarios.hook: You can't tell what you're feeling, it's just 'big'.

options.text: Try naming a few: "mad? sad? worried?"
options.consequence: One name fits; the big feeling gets clearer.

options.text: Give up and stay upset
options.consequence: The cloudy feeling stays confusing.

scenarios.debrief: Trying out feeling-words helps you find the right one.
scenarios.relearn: If a feeling is fuzzy, try a few names until one fits.

scenarios.hook: A friend says "don't cry, that's silly."

yourLine.text: "It's okay to cry. Crying helps."
Agree and hold the tears in

scenarios.relearn: You can remind a friend that crying is okay.

scenarios.hook: Build a breathing pattern to use anytime.
scenarios.relearn: In slow, tiny hold, out slow, your calming breath.

scenarios.hook: You see someone left out and looking sad at the park.

options.text: Invite them: "want to play?"
options.consequence: Their sad feeling lifts; you made a friend.

options.text: Carry on without them
options.consequence: They stay sad and alone.

scenarios.debrief: Noticing a sad feeling and acting kindly is real empathy.
scenarios.relearn: You can lift someone's sad feeling by including them.

scenarios.hook: "You shouldn't bother grown-ups with your feelings."

myth.un: You shouldn't bother grown-ups with your feelings.
myth.re: Trusted grown-ups want to help with your feelings.
myth.why: Helping you is their job and joy.

scenarios.relearn: Trusted grown-ups are glad to help with your feelings.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: being kind to yourself when you feel bad helps. Agree?
scenarios.affirm: Yes, being gentle with yourself helps big feelings settle.
scenarios.relearn: Being kind to yourself helps you through hard feelings.

scenarios.hook: Sort the feelings into 'comfy' and 'uncomfy' (both okay!).
scenarios.relearn: Comfy and uncomfy feelings are all okay to have.

scenarios.hook: You feel embarrassed after a mistake in front of friends.

options.text: Tell yourself "everyone makes mistakes, it's okay"
options.consequence: The embarrassment fades faster.

options.text: Decide everyone hates you
options.consequence: You feel worse over a normal slip.

scenarios.debrief: Embarrassment is okay and passes; mistakes are normal.
scenarios.relearn: Embarrassment is okay; everyone makes mistakes.

scenarios.hook: Match the calmer to where you might use it.
scenarios.relearn: You have calmers for every place and every size of feeling.

scenarios.hook: Your friend is proud of something they made.

yourLine.text: "Wow, you must feel so proud!"
"It's not that great."

scenarios.relearn: Naming a friend's happy feeling makes it even bigger.

scenarios.hook: You feel a feeling so big it's scary.

options.text: Breathe, then tell a trusted grown-up
options.consequence: You're not alone; together it feels manageable.

options.text: Try to handle it all alone
options.consequence: It stays overwhelming.

scenarios.debrief: Really big feelings are easier with a grown-up's help.
scenarios.relearn: For very big feelings: breathe, then tell a trusted grown-up.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: your feelings are like friends, even the tricky ones. Treat them kindly?
scenarios.affirm: Your feelings are part of you; treating them kindly helps you thrive.
scenarios.relearn: All your feelings are part of you and deserve kindness.

scenarios.hook: Last feelings to name. Match the face to the word.
scenarios.relearn: Proud, confused, calm, more feelings you can name.

scenarios.hook: Sort: the feeling, or the action? (Remember: feelings okay, some actions not.)
scenarios.relearn: Feelings are always okay; we still choose kind actions.

scenarios.hook: You're frustrated with a puzzle that won't work.

options.text: Breathe, then try again or ask for help
options.consequence: You calm down and often crack it.

options.text: Throw the puzzle
options.consequence: It's still not done and now you're crosser.

scenarios.debrief: Frustration is okay; breathe and try again (links Can-Do Kids).
scenarios.relearn: When frustrated, breathe and try again or ask for help.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a kind feelings-friend move, or not?

items.text: Copying their sad voice to mock

scenarios.relearn: Listening, sharing and including are kind; teasing and ignoring aren't.

scenarios.hook: Practise your big, clear 'no'.
scenarios.setup: Loud and proud (not shouting, just strong):

yourLine.text: "No. I don't want to."
A tiny whisper, then give in

scenarios.relearn: A clear, calm 'no' is a feelings-and-safety superpower.

scenarios.hook: Build today's feelings check-in.
scenarios.prompt: Pick your feeling and one thing that helps.
scenarios.relearn: A check-in: name your feeling, a calmer, and who you can tell.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: which calmer will you try next time a feeling gets big?
scenarios.affirm: Great pick. Having a plan makes big feelings less scary.
scenarios.relearn: Having a go-to calmer makes big feelings easier.

scenarios.hook: Capstone: two friends both need you, one's sad, one's excited.

options.text: Comfort the sad one, then celebrate with the happy one
options.consequence: Both feel seen; you're a great feelings friend.

options.text: Only join the fun one
options.consequence: The sad friend feels forgotten.

scenarios.debrief: A good feelings friend makes room for everyone's feelings.
scenarios.relearn: You can care for different friends' feelings, one at a time.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: say it with me, all feelings are...?
scenarios.affirm: All feelings are okay. It's what we do with them that we choose.
scenarios.relearn: All feelings are okay; we choose kind actions.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: you've met all the Feelings Friends. How do you feel?
scenarios.affirm: You're a true Feelings Friend now, to others and to yourself.
scenarios.relearn: You can name, calm and share feelings, and help others too.

scenarios.hook: Lensy: who is one grown-up you'd tell about a big feeling?
scenarios.affirm: Keep that person in mind, they're part of your feelings team.
scenarios.relearn: You have grown-ups on your feelings team; know who they are.

scenarios.hook: Start your day the Feelings Friend way.

yourLine.text: "Good morning feeling, I see you, you're okay."
Pretend I don't feel anything

scenarios.relearn: Greeting your feelings each day keeps you their friend.

scenarios.hook: "Brave kids never get scared."

myth.un: Brave kids never get scared.
myth.re: Brave kids feel scared and try anyway.
myth.why: Feeling scared is what makes a thing brave to do.

scenarios.relearn: Feeling scared and being brave can both be true at once.

scenarios.hook: "Only babies cry at drop-off."

myth.un: Only babies cry at drop-off.
myth.re: Anyone can cry when they miss someone.
myth.why: Missing your family is a big feeling for every age.

scenarios.relearn: Crying when you miss someone is okay for any kid.

scenarios.hook: "Big kids shouldn't feel shy."

myth.un: Big kids shouldn't feel shy.
myth.re: Feeling shy is okay; it just means new feels new.
myth.why: Shy is your body taking a moment to feel safe.

scenarios.relearn: Feeling shy is okay; you can warm up at your own pace.

scenarios.hook: "You shouldn't feel sad about a small thing."

myth.un: You shouldn't feel sad about a small thing.
myth.re: Any size thing can give you a real feeling.
myth.why: Your feeling is true even if the thing looks small.

scenarios.relearn: It's okay to feel sad, even about something small.

scenarios.hook: "Feeling jealous makes you a mean kid."

myth.un: Feeling jealous makes you a mean kid.
myth.re: Jealousy is a feeling, not a mean thing you did.
myth.why: A feeling is never unkind; only an action can be.

scenarios.relearn: Jealousy is okay to feel; you still choose a kind action.

scenarios.hook: "Boys shouldn't feel scared of the dark."

myth.un: Boys shouldn't feel scared of the dark.
myth.re: Any kid can feel scared of the dark.
myth.why: Being scared is a feeling for everyone, not one gender.

scenarios.relearn: Feeling scared is okay for any kid, any gender.

scenarios.hook: "Girls shouldn't stomp when they're cross."

myth.un: Girls shouldn't stomp when they're cross.
myth.re: Anyone can feel cross; we pick a safe way to show it.
myth.why: Anger belongs to everyone; the action is the choice.

scenarios.relearn: Anger is okay for everyone; we choose a safe way to show it.

scenarios.hook: "You have to feel happy at your own birthday."

myth.un: You have to feel happy at your own birthday.
myth.re: You can feel any way, even on a happy day.
myth.why: Nobody can make a feeling happen on a schedule.

scenarios.relearn: It's okay to feel any way, even on a happy day.

scenarios.hook: "Feeling two feelings at once is wrong."

myth.un: Feeling two feelings at once is wrong.
myth.re: You can feel happy and nervous at the same time.
myth.why: More than one feeling can share your heart at once.

scenarios.relearn: Feeling more than one feeling at once is okay.

scenarios.hook: "Asking for a hug when sad is babyish."

myth.un: Asking for a hug when sad is babyish.
myth.re: Asking for a hug is a kind, strong way to feel better.
myth.why: Reaching out for comfort helps a big feeling settle.

scenarios.relearn: Asking for a hug when you're sad is okay and strong.

scenarios.hook: "You should be over it by now."

myth.un: You should be over it by now.
myth.re: Feelings take the time they take.
myth.why: A feeling shrinks at its own pace, not on a clock.

scenarios.relearn: A feeling can last a while, and that's okay.

scenarios.hook: "Feeling left out means nobody likes you."

myth.un: Feeling left out means nobody likes you.
myth.re: Feeling left out is a real feeling, not a fact about you.
myth.why: A feeling tells you how you feel, not what's true of you.

scenarios.relearn: Feeling left out is okay; it isn't a fact about you.

scenarios.hook: "Happy kids never feel grumpy."

myth.un: Happy kids never feel grumpy.
myth.re: A happy kid can still have a grumpy moment.
myth.why: One feeling now doesn't cancel another one later.

scenarios.relearn: Even a happy kid feels grumpy sometimes, and that's okay.

scenarios.hook: "You shouldn't feel nervous on the first day."

myth.un: You shouldn't feel nervous on the first day.
myth.re: Feeling nervous about something new is normal.
myth.why: New things often bring a flutter, and that's okay.

scenarios.relearn: Feeling nervous about a new place is okay for anyone.

scenarios.hook: "Crying means you can't fix it yourself."

myth.un: Crying means you can't fix it yourself.
myth.re: Crying lets a big feeling out so you can think.
myth.why: Tears are a release, not a sign you gave up.

scenarios.relearn: Crying lets big feelings out; it helps you, not weakens you.

scenarios.hook: "Being excited and loud is naughty."

myth.un: Being excited and loud is naughty.
myth.re: Excited is a happy feeling; we find a safe place for it.
myth.why: The feeling is fine; we just pick where the loud goes.

scenarios.relearn: Excited is okay; we choose a kind, safe way to show it.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a comfy feeling, or an uncomfy one? (Both are okay to have!)
scenarios.relearn: Comfy or uncomfy, every feeling is okay to have.

scenarios.hook: Sort: a kind way, or unkind way, to show being cross?

items.text: Stomp your feet on the floor

scenarios.relearn: You can show being cross in safe ways that hurt nobody.

scenarios.hook: A myth about feelings.

myth.un: Feelings are too hard for little kids to name.
myth.re: Even little kids can learn feeling words and name them.
myth.why: Naming a feeling is a skill you practise, and it makes the feeling smaller.

scenarios.relearn: Even little kids can name feelings, name it to tame it.

scenarios.hook: A myth about big feelings.

myth.un: If you name a sad feeling, it gets bigger.
myth.re: Naming a feeling actually helps it get smaller.
myth.why: Putting a feeling into words gives your brain a way to settle it.

scenarios.relearn: Naming a feeling makes it smaller, not bigger.

scenarios.hook: A myth about feeling two things.

myth.un: You can only feel one feeling at a time.
myth.re: You can feel two feelings at the same time.
myth.why: Like being excited and nervous at once, more than one feeling can share a moment.

scenarios.relearn: You can feel more than one feeling at the same time.

scenarios.hook: A myth about reading faces.

myth.un: You can never tell how someone feels.
myth.re: You can often tell by looking at their face and body.
myth.why: A smile, tears, or a scrunched face are clues to how a person feels.

scenarios.relearn: Reading a face and body helps you know how someone feels.

scenarios.hook: A myth about who feels what.

myth.un: Only some kinds of children feel scared or cry.
myth.re: Every child feels scared and cries sometimes.
myth.why: All feelings belong to everyone, no feeling is only for one kind of child.

scenarios.relearn: Every feeling is for everyone, no feeling belongs to one kind of child.

scenarios.hook: A myth about checking in on yourself.

myth.un: There's a wrong answer when you say how you feel.
myth.re: There's no wrong answer when you check in on yourself.
myth.why: Whatever you feel right now is real and okay to name.

scenarios.relearn: Checking in on yourself has no wrong answer.

scenarios.hook: A myth about grown-ups.

myth.un: Grown-ups don't really have feelings.
myth.re: Grown-ups feel every kind of feeling too.
myth.why: Even Amma, Appa, and Lensy feel happy, sad, scared, and angry sometimes.

scenarios.relearn: Everyone, even grown-ups, feels every kind of feeling sometimes.

scenarios.hook: A myth about feeling words.

myth.un: There are only a few feelings, like happy and sad.
myth.re: There are many feelings, each with its own name.
myth.why: Excited, jealous, shy, calm, proud, and more are all feelings you can name.

scenarios.relearn: There are many feelings, and learning the words is the whole point.
